body:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: model-warmup-failure pool-a - high error rate on model load. Paging oncall SRE.

sre-jordan: got the page, jumping in. which customers affected? trying to pull logs now.

engineer-leah: seeing repeated OOM during model deserialization on node gpu-az2-17. stack shows allocation failure inside cuMemAlloc.

engineer-leah: logs excerpt:
```
2024-06-20T14:00:12.842Z ERROR warmup: model_id=rw-2.1.0 load_step=deserialize err=std::bad_alloc at 0x7f8c...
2024-06-20T14:00:12.843Z ERROR runtime: cuda: cuMemAlloc failed: out of memory (cudaErrorMemoryAllocation)
2024-06-20T14:00:12.843Z WARN warmup: compile cache miss, falling back to on-the-fly compile
```

sre-jordan: thanks, Leah. infra-maya can you confirm node memory usage and if any other pods hogging GPU?

infra-maya: checking nvidia-smi and kube top. gpu-az2-17 shows 98% GPU mem used by orphaned process from previous failed warmup. PID 2431 (python). I can kill and restart the pod, but worried about stampede if we restart many pods at once.

eng-ryan: we have aggressive parallel warmup settings for Dedicated pools (concurrency=6). if multiple pods attempt load concurrently they OOM. we should reduce concurrency and use staggered backoff.

engineer-leah: agree. proposed immediate mitigation: 1) pause warmup for pool-a via control plane flag 2) kill orphan process 3) reduce warmup concurrency to 1 and force sequential warmup 4) route new loads to fallback variant rw-2.0-quant for customers while we stabilize.

infra-maya: killing orphaned PID 2431 now.

engineer-leah: patch applied to warmup config: concurrency=1 for pool-a. sending rolling restart to warmup controllers with graceful 45s drain.

product-anya: customer impact? any external errors showing up in SLO dashboards?

cs-ben: saw an alert from customer "FinEdge" about 503s on their inference endpoints starting 14:01 UTC. They've reported about 22 minutes of elevated error rates (14:01-14:23). I'm messaging them PRIORITY update.

sre-jordan: ok, put a short public note: "experiencing model load errors, routing to fallback models, mitigations in progress". keep it short.

cs-ben: sent to FinEdge: "We observed model warmup failures in pool-a causing intermittent 503s. We have routed traffic to a compatible quantized variant and are applying configuration fixes. ETA stabilization 10-15m. Will update."

engineer-leah: after killing orphan, next load attempts succeed for some nodes but we still see compile timeouts on a subset. compile cache looks corrupted on two nodes. I will evict compile cache and restart runtime there.

engineer-leah: run command to evict cache: ```kubectl exec -n redwood runtime-controller -- rm -rf /var/local/compile-cache/* && systemctl restart redwood-runtime```

infra-maya: doing evict+restart on gpu-az2-17 and gpu-az2-19 sequentially.

sre-jordan: while infra restarts, enable routing fallback rule to prefer rw-2.0-quant for pool-a in routing-layer.

eng-ryan: pushed routing change: prefer_variant=rw-2.0-quant, fallback_timeout=500ms. Also lowered warmup concurrency cluster-wide to 2 until we validate fix.

incident-bot: Note: config-change detected by audit (user eng-ryan).

engineer-leah: post-evict logs show successful load on previously failing node. snippet:
```
2024-06-20T14:07:39.112Z INFO warmup: model_id=rw-2.1.0 load complete sequence=1 memory_used=12.3GB
2024-06-20T14:07:39.113Z INFO runtime: serving ready model=rw-2.1.0 node=gpu-az2-17
```

cs-ben: FinEdge on call confirmed reduced 503s, latency improved. they still see occasional 500s for a couple routes.

product-anya: any risk of regression if we keep quantized fallback longer? we need to preserve output quality metrics.

eng-ryan: quantized variant is slightly lower quality on edge cases; we should keep it as short-term mitigation. starting canary to re-enable rw-2.1.0 for 5% traffic after all nodes show healthy warmups and compile cache cleared.

sre-jordan: canary enabled at 5% at 14:12 UTC. monitoring metrics and token-level errors.

engineer-leah: canary warmups succeeded on 4/4 nodes. metrics show no OOMs for 20m.

incident-bot: Incident status: acknowledged -> mitigated (partial). Triggering page to oncall to confirm if we can declare mitigated.

sre-jordan: declaring incident mitigated at 14:30 UTC. root cause: aggressive parallel warmup + stale compile cache + orphaned runtime process holding GPU memory causing OOM during deserialization and subsequent compile timeout fallback.

infra-maya: follow-ups: add eviction cron for stale runtime processes, add liveness probe to kill long-running orphan loads.

eng-ryan: follow-ups: make warmup concurrency adaptive based on free-GPU-memory signal, add canary warmup first policy to avoid stampedes, extend compile-cache health checks and fallback to safe quantized compile path instead of on-the-fly full compile.

product-anya: coordinate customer communications: post short incident summary to FinEdge and update status page with note about mitigation and next-day postmortem.

cs-ben: FinEdge escalated but satisfied with mitigation. I'll schedule a follow-up SLO review with them.

sre-jordan: logging ticket: INC-2024-729. assign owners: eng-ryan (warmup changes), infra-maya (eviction/liveness), engineer-leah (compile-cache recovery tooling), cs-ben (customer comms), product-anya (postmortem writeup). ETA for fixes: 48-72h.

engineer-leah: adding PR with tests for sequential warmup and simulated low-memory to prevent regressions. link: https://git.redwood.dev/rw/warmup/pull/482

eng-ryan: thanks team. closing thread after postmortem. :white_check_mark:
